question.text: Rajesh invested INR 50 lakh in an AIF. He has received distributions of INR 30 lakh. The DPI is:

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = cumulative Distributions / Paid-In Capital = 30 / 50 = 0.6x. Rajesh has received back 60% of his investment so far; he needs additional distributions (DPI to reach 1.0x or above) to recover his full paid-in capital. The Trap: A DPI below 1.0x does not on its own mean the investment is bad — the fund may still hold significant unrealised value (RVPI) that can be distributed later as the portfolio is exited. DPI should be read alongside RVPI and TVPI rather than in isolation. Note: The earlier explanation included year-by-year normal/on-track/concerning lifecycle benchmarks (year 3 of a 7-year fund etc.) that were not supported by the checked workbook pages. Those unsourced lifecycle claims have been removed; only the DPI calculation and the early-stage J-curve caveat actually grounded in the source are retained.
